subprocess_flow.substep_name: Triage Security Tier & Execute Fast-Track Determination
subprocess_flow.description: Assess the incoming AI system architecture, data classification level, and proposed deployment model against calibrated Ministry of Justice cybersecurity risk tier criteria. The cyber security team determines whether the workload qualifies for automated fast-track static analysis or requires full-scope manual adversarial evaluation, logging the decision in the enterprise risk management portal to prevent engineering bottlenecks for low-risk systems.
subprocess_flow.responsible_party: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) & Cyber Security Team
success_criteria: Fast-track eligibility determination recorded and signed off
Cybersecurity review scope and testing horizon established
Zero intake queueing delays for low-risk automation workloads
subprocess_flow.purpose: Calibrate cybersecurity evaluation rigor against system risk tier to ensure resource-efficient security oversight without delaying delivery.
subprocess_flow.scope: All AI initiatives submitted for architectural and security baseline review across the MoJ.
subprocess_flow.process_owner: MoJ Chief Enterprise Architect & Head of Data Governance
triggers: Completion of data quality validation and submission of system architecture documentation
end_conditions: Formal determination logged authorizing either expedited automated clearance or full in-depth review

step_risks_and_controls.risk: Misclassification of a complex judicial AI system as low risk to qualify for expedited review
step_risks_and_controls.control: Mandatory CISO peer validation of fast-track eligibility against statutory high-risk criteria

change_management.change_request_process: Appeals against fast-track eligibility determinations must be submitted to the Lead Security Architect
change_management.versioning_rules: Triage determination records linked semantically to system architecture Git commit hash

improvement_inputs: Triage dispute and re-classification incidence rates

subprocess_flow.substep_name: Review Infrastructure as Code & Architecture Baseline
subprocess_flow.description: Inspect Infrastructure as Code (IaC) templates, network topologies, orchestration scripts, and deployment blueprints against MoJ Secure by Design baselines and NIST SP 800-53 controls. Automated static code analysis tools (checkov and tfsec) run within CI/CD security pipelines to detect misconfigurations, open egress paths, and unsecured container configurations before cloud infrastructure provisioning.
subprocess_flow.responsible_party: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) & Cyber Security Team
dependencies: Triage Security Tier & Execute Fast-Track Determination
success_criteria: IaC templates conform 100% to MoJ Secure by Design baseline rules
Zero unmitigated critical or high infrastructure misconfigurations
Security Architecture Approval Record signed and committed to repository
subprocess_flow.purpose: Verify that foundational cloud infrastructure and compute configurations adhere strictly to MoJ security baselines.
subprocess_flow.scope: Terraform, CloudFormation, Helm charts, container orchestration, and network routing configurations.
subprocess_flow.process_owner: MoJ Chief Enterprise Architect & Head of Data Governance
triggers: Approval of calibrated security fast-track determination and provisioning of IaC code repositories
end_conditions: Formal issuance of Security Architecture Approval Record confirming IaC baseline conformance

step_risks_and_controls.risk: Flawed IaC configurations provisioning public endpoints or unsegmented subnet access to justice data
step_risks_and_controls.control: Automated checkov and tfsec scanning gates enforcing build breaks on critical misconfigurations

change_management.change_request_process: IaC baseline deviations require formal exception approval from the CISO Technical Review Panel
change_management.versioning_rules: IaC repositories versioned using semantic git tags and cryptographically signed commits

improvement_inputs: MoJ Secure by Design pattern updates

subprocess_flow.substep_name: Assess COTS Vendor Security & Cloud Supply Chain
subprocess_flow.description: Perform comprehensive third-party vendor risk assessments for Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) AI solutions, Foundation Model APIs, and hosted SaaS components. The cyber security team verifies external SOC2 Type II attestations, ISO 27001 certifications, multi-tenant isolation architectures, sub-processor security guarantees, and contractual commitments regarding zero data retention for model training.
subprocess_flow.responsible_party: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) & Cyber Security Team
inputs: Vendor SOC2 Type II / ISO 27001 Audits
dependencies: Triage Security Tier & Execute Fast-Track Determination
success_criteria: Valid SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications verified for all external SaaS/COTS vendors
Third-party zero data retention and enterprise enclave isolation legally confirmed
Vendor Cloud Security Review signed off with zero open vendor security exceptions
subprocess_flow.purpose: Ensure third-party AI vendors and hosted Foundation Model services meet HMG public sector cloud security standards.
subprocess_flow.scope: All third-party SaaS platforms, COTS AI packages, and external Foundation Model API endpoints.
subprocess_flow.process_owner: MoJ Chief Enterprise Architect & Head of Data Governance
triggers: Identification of external SaaS, COTS, or Foundation Model endpoints within system architecture
end_conditions: Publication of approved Vendor Security Assessment Dossier and Vendor Cloud Security Review

step_risks_and_controls.risk: Third-party vendor data compromise or unauthorized use of justice data for model training
step_risks_and_controls.control: Contractual and technical verification of zero-data-retention APIs and enterprise private tenant agreements

governance_requirements: Crown Commercial Service AI Procurement Guidance

change_management.change_request_process: Introduction of new third-party vendors or sub-processors requires CISO supply chain review
change_management.versioning_rules: Vendor security dossiers versioned annually or upon audit attestation expiry

subprocess_flow.substep_name: Perform AI Threat Modeling & OWASP LLM Assessment
subprocess_flow.description: Construct an AI-specific threat model applying STRIDE, NIST AI RMF GOVERN/PROTECT, and OWASP Top 10 for LLM frameworks. Cyber security specialists analyze prompt injection defense architectures, direct/indirect adversarial injection vectors, model inversion risks, training data extraction, and excessive agency in agentic pipelines, documenting counter-measures within the threat mitigation matrix.
subprocess_flow.responsible_party: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) & Cyber Security Team
outputs: OWASP LLM Top 10 Threat Mitigation Assessment
Generative AI Threat & Prompt Injection Defense Review
dependencies: Review Infrastructure as Code & Architecture Baseline
success_criteria: AI Threat Model fully documented covering STRIDE and NIST AI RMF categories
100% of OWASP Top 10 LLM risks evaluated with explicit mitigating controls
Prompt injection firewall specifications verified against adversarial exploit vectors
subprocess_flow.purpose: Identify, categorize, and establish technical mitigations for AI-specific attack surfaces and generative vulnerability vectors.
subprocess_flow.scope: Inference endpoints, prompt pipelines, RAG retrieval layers, vector databases, and model interfaces.
subprocess_flow.process_owner: MoJ Chief Enterprise Architect & Head of Data Governance
triggers: Availability of finalized data flow diagrams and prompt injection defense specifications
end_conditions: Threat modeling report and mitigation matrix approved and signed off by lead cyber architect

step_risks_and_controls.risk: Prompt injection exploits leading to unauthorized execution, jailbreaking, or sensitive record extraction
step_risks_and_controls.control: Implementation of input/output guardrails (e.g., NeMo Guardrails) and semantic prompt firewalls

governance_requirements: OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications
NIST AI RMF - GOVERN & PROTECT Functions

change_management.change_request_process: Prompt defense policy updates or threat model re-scopes submitted via security sprint backlog
change_management.versioning_rules: Threat models and mitigation matrices version-controlled in git as markdown and architectural diagrams

improvement_inputs: UK AI Safety Institute vulnerability reports

subprocess_flow.substep_name: Validate Enclave Boundaries, Encryption & Egress Controls
subprocess_flow.description: Execute deep technical verification of cryptographic protection, network segmentation, and API egress boundaries. The security team validates KMS envelope encryption using customer-managed keys (CMK), FIPS 140-3 compliance, mTLS across microservices, strict VPC PrivateLink perimeters, and outbound egress filtering preventing unauthorized data leakage from Foundation Model inference endpoints.
subprocess_flow.responsible_party: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) & Cyber Security Team
dependencies: Review Infrastructure as Code & Architecture Baseline
Perform AI Threat Modeling & OWASP LLM Assessment
success_criteria: KMS envelope encryption verified with customer-managed keys for all data at rest
mTLS 1.3 enforced across all inter-service and API communications
Zero unrestricted internet egress routes from secure cloud enclaves processing OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE data
subprocess_flow.purpose: Guarantee robust cryptographic integrity, enclave isolation, and strict boundary egress controls for justice sector data.
subprocess_flow.scope: KMS key policies, TLS termination endpoints, VPC peering, firewall egress filter configurations, and network security groups.
subprocess_flow.process_owner: MoJ Chief Enterprise Architect & Head of Data Governance
triggers: Completion of IaC baseline review and security architecture approval
end_conditions: Formal passing validation log signed confirming encryption standards and perimeter isolation

step_risks_and_controls.risk: OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE offender data exfiltrated via unmonitored outbound API egress routes
step_risks_and_controls.control: Enforcement of private endpoint routing, strict domain allow-listing, and egress proxy inspection

change_management.change_request_process: Cryptographic key policy or firewall rule adjustments require CISO Security Architecture sign-off
change_management.versioning_rules: KMS and firewall configurations version-controlled in GitOps repository

subprocess_flow.description: Deploy specialized penetration testers and ethical red teams to conduct targeted adversarial testing against staged AI endpoints, data pipelines, and orchestration planes. Testing exercises include prompt injection bypasses, API brute-forcing, jailbreak evaluations, token extraction, container escape tests, and adversarial evasion attacks in a staging environment mirroring production.
subprocess_flow.responsible_party: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) & Cyber Security Team
inputs: OWASP LLM Top 10 Threat Mitigation Assessment
dependencies: Validate Enclave Boundaries, Encryption & Egress Controls
success_criteria: Zero open critical or high severity vulnerabilities verified upon test completion
All identified moderate findings logged with remediation owners and target timelines
Adversarial prompt injection testing confirms robustness of runtime guardrails
subprocess_flow.purpose: Empirically discover and remediate exploitable security vulnerabilities prior to production deployment.
subprocess_flow.scope: Staged inference APIs, container runtime hosts, prompt firewalls, vector stores, and administrative interfaces.
subprocess_flow.process_owner: MoJ Chief Enterprise Architect & Head of Data Governance
triggers: Successful validation of cryptographic boundaries and deployment to secure staging environment
end_conditions: Formal publication and sign-off of Penetration Testing Summary with all criticals resolved

step_risks_and_controls.risk: Critical zero-day exploits or unmitigated adversarial attack vectors in production inference
step_risks_and_controls.control: Mandatory red-team penetration testing and pre-release vulnerability remediation gates

governance_requirements: NIST SP 800-115 Technical Guide to Information Security Testing

change_management.change_request_process: Vulnerability remediation commits tracked in Jira/ServiceNow and validated via re-test scans
change_management.versioning_rules: Penetration test findings cataloged under MoJ Defect Management System with build IDs

subprocess_flow.description: Synthesize findings from the IaC review, vendor security assessment, AI threat model, encryption verification, and penetration testing summary into the comprehensive MoJ Secure by Design AI Compliance Review dossier. The CISO and Cyber Security Team formally review residual risk registers and issue the cryptographically signed Security Sign-off Certificate permitting system progression to ethical review.

outputs: MoJ Secure by Design AI Compliance Review
dependencies: Assess COTS Vendor Security & Cloud Supply Chain
success_criteria: 100% of required security artifacts consolidated and archived in immutable governance repository
Zero open critical or high cybersecurity risks verified
Cryptographically signed Security Sign-off Certificate issued and registered
subprocess_flow.purpose: Provide authoritative cybersecurity certification confirming that the AI solution complies with MoJ Secure by Design principles.
subprocess_flow.scope: Final security compliance review dossier, residual risk registers, and formal certification records.
subprocess_flow.process_owner: MoJ Chief Enterprise Architect & Head of Data Governance

UK Central Digital and Data Office (CDDO) Service Standard
